title: Latency signature indexer and adaptive noise-filtering pipeline for SLO alerts
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Summary: Build a latency-signature indexing stage and adaptive noise-filtering layer in the metrics/log/tracing pipeline to reduce SLO alert fatigue, improve burn-rate accuracy, and provide deterministic trace links on latency dashboards. This ticket covers design, implementation, dashboarding, and rollout of: (1) lightweight tracing hooks to tag requests with route/model metadata and sampling hints, (2) an indexer that computes compact 'latency signatures' (fingerprints) for traces and stores counts/time-series, (3) a noise-filtering step that suppresses low-confidence metric spikes (rate-limited and correlated across signals), and (4) new dashboards + alert policies that use signature-based anomaly attribution to decide paging and burn-rate escalation.

Motivation: Recent oncall noise analysis (see incident-notes) shows ~30% of burn-rate alerts are short-lived spikes with no customer observable impact and high false-positive rates. Causes are transient backend retries, telemetry duplication from frontend SDK v1.3, and uneven sampling of traces. By extracting recurring latency signatures and enforcing cross-signal correlation, we can avoid paging for cheap, noisy events while preserving true degradation detection.

Goals:
- Reduce actionable pager triggers from burn-rate alerts by >=40% for latency SLOs in the next quarter.
- Provide an index of recurring latency signatures for easier RCA and automated grouping in dashboards.
- Ensure new tracing hooks add <=1% p99 latency overhead on critical RPC paths.
- Maintain backwards-compatible metric schemas and allow feature flag-controlled rollout per org.

Technical approach:
1) Tracing Hooks: add light-weight hook points in request routers to attach: route_id, model_variant, customer_tier, preliminary latency buckets, and sampling_hint. Hooks implemented in the serving runtime (C++) with a thin protobuf header emitted to the tracing agent; language SDK adapters (Go/Python/Node) will forward the same headers.
2) Signature extraction: in the trace enrichment service (collector), compute compact signatures using a deterministic hash over sampled span latencies, error flags, and route/model tags. The signature includes a versioned schema so we can iterate. Signatures are stored in ClickHouse/TSDB as time-series counts and example trace IDs.
3) Noise-filter stage: a streaming processor (Kafka -> Flink/Beam) runs sliding-window aggregation and applies filters: duplicate suppression (x-forwarded dedupe), burst dampening (min-duration & min-count thresholds), cross-signal correlation (metric+log+trace) and adaptive thresholds based on historical baseline percentiles. Filtering decisions are annotated and emitted to the alert scoring engine.
4) Alert scoring & paging policy integration: augment burn-rate alert evaluation to include signature-based impact score and correlation score. Update paging policies: low-impact signatures and non-correlated spikes trigger team-only async notifications; correlated multi-signal anomalies or signatures with high customer_impact force normal paging.
5) Dashboards & RCA UX: create a "Signature Explorer" Grafana panel listing top signatures, counts, sample traces, and links to trace viewer. Update latency/error dashboards with per-signature heatmaps and a timeline of signature emergence.

Schema & compatibility: Schema v1 for signatures: signature_id (string), signature_version, route_id, model_variant(optional), window_count, samples (list of trace ids), first_seen_ts, last_seen_ts. Stored as flattened strings in the ticket artifact and in ClickHouse columns. Emit migration docs; default behavior is opt-in per org via feature flag.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for signature hashing and dedupe logic.
- Canary on internal staging with 5% sample traffic (canary orgs: internal-dev, alpha-corp).
- Backtest historical 90-day metrics to estimate reduction in false positives before rollout.
- Perf benchmark to ensure hook overhead <1% p99 and ingestion pipeline cost within 10% of current.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Signature extractor produces stable signature IDs for identical trace patterns across 95% of cases.
2) Noise-filtered burn-rate alerts in staging reduce pager triggers by >=40% in backtest.
3) Tracing hook overhead <=1% p99 measured in perf harness.
4) Dashboards show signature counts and provide trace links; alert policy references signature impact score.
5) Feature flag enables per-org opt-in/out without schema breakage.
implementation_notes:
- Tracing hooks: modify runtime hook registry (serving/runtime/hook_registry) and SDK adapters (sdks/*).
- Collector: add signature plugin to trace-enricher service (enricher/plugins/signature).
- Streaming processor: extend existing pipeline (observability/stream/pipeline) with signature-filter stage.
- Alerting: update alert-evaluator to accept signature/correlation scores.
- Storage: ClickHouse table observability.signatures_v1; retention 90d, partitioned by date+route.
- Telemetry: emit metric observability.signature.ingest.latency and observability.signature.suppressed_count.
- Feature flagging: console feature toggles + org-level flag in platform configs.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: signature collisions or over-generalization leading to missed regressions. Mitigation: versioned signature schema, conservative thresholds in initial rollout, manual override to force paging when in doubt.
Risk: increased ingestion cost. Mitigation: sample only when baseline anomaly probability > threshold, compress signature payloads, and shard counts to ClickHouse daily partitions.
Risk: SDK adoption lag. Mitigation: server-side best-effort tagging using inferred route/model where SDK headers absent and gradual SDK rollout plan with metrics to track adoption.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary, 2 weeks): enable hooks in internal staging, signature extraction on 5% sample traffic, backtest and tune filters.
Phase 2 (org opt-in, 4 weeks): enable for select customers (internal-dev, alpha-corp, beta-tenant), monitor suppressed_count and missed-alerts, collect feedback.
Phase 3 (gradual global enable, 6 weeks): progressive ramp to 100% using burn-rate safety gates and rollback if missed-alert ratio > 0.5% vs baseline.
Phase 4 (cleanup): migrate signatures to longer retention for RCA & iterate signature schema v2.
